$comment: The source of sf-contents's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js), in the 1.4 form (scripts/generate-component-files.mjs writes rule.js, aliases.json, studio.fixture.json, studio.scenario.json, probe.json and smart.manifest.json from it). A new component, made against standard simai.smart-component 1.3.11 and vocabulary 1.1.5; the design target is tab 1 of ui-control prototypes/docara-four.html (owner-approved 2026-10-30).

layout.summary: How the contents are laid out (the axis of sf-dropdown and sf-empty-state: view is a reserved name, §3.1). column: a side list with the current section's bar; sheet: one button showing the current section and the reading progress, opening the list; rail: short strokes at the edge, the names on hover and focus, and on a tap where nothing hovers; bar: a sticky row of anchor tabs, for long forms, what does not fit in «Ещё (n)» (overflow); auto: column at and above the collapse step, sheet below it (a media rule, so the first paint is right without the script). Below md (44rem) the sheet view's list opens as a bottom sheet. For an article on a phone, a column with sticky="false" at the top of the text is the contents once, in place. The old value compact is a dated alias of sheet until 2027-01-01 (owner decision C134: compact means density only; noted in SF.deprecations, journal value-contents-layout-compact-to-sheet)

collapse.summary: With layout auto: the Framework breakpoint (sm 32rem, md 44rem, lg 60rem, xl 72rem) below which the column turns into the sheet

target.summary: A CSS selector of the content whose headings make the contents, when no items are given; empty: the page's main, else its body. The headings found get an id when they have none

levels.summary: The heading levels collected from the target: one level (2) or a range (2-3). A deeper level is indented

items.x-markup: the JSON island (data-sf-settings) or the property; without items, links written inside the element (<a href="#id" data-level="3">) are the items, and without those the headings of the target
items.summary: The sections, [{id, text, level?, count?, status?}], when a server knows them: the element then collects nothing and spies on the elements with these ids. level is the heading level (2 when not given). count (a number above 0) and status (error, warning or success) put a badge on the entry's line, sized by its text (sf-badge line="text"), and say it in the entry's name («Контакты: 2 ошибки»); a section marked error is chosen to its first invalid field, not its heading (owner decision C95 point 6, CT-07). Links written inside carry them as data-count and data-status

size.summary: The ladder rung of the text and of the sheet view's controls

sticky.summary: Every layout stays in view while the page scrolls (position sticky, below --sf-contents-inset-block-start): the column, the rail, the bar, and the sheet's button, which takes the page surface as its backing so nothing shows through it

line.summary: Who draws the line the entries stand on, in the column and the bar (owner decision C95 point 1, CT-01): own (the default) -- the element draws its 1 px line; edge -- the host's divider is the line: the element draws none and the current section's 2 px mark lies on its inline-start edge (the bar: its bottom edge), over the divider's pixel, so the host puts it flush against its divider (an inset shadow or a border on the column, the element its first child); none -- no line and no mark, the current section is its ink and weight alone. The text's distance from the line is --sf-contents-inset-inline

expand.summary: Which deeper entries the column and the sheet's list show (owner decision C95 point 3, CT-11): all (the default) every level; current only the deeper entries of the current branch -- the top-level section being read and the entries under it -- the other branches folded to their top entry, as a long documentation page needs. The rail and the bar show every entry

overflow.summary: With layout bar, what the row does with sections that do not fit: more (the default) puts them whole into a trailing «Ещё (n)» menu in their order, the current one always staying in the row, as sf-tabs does (owner decision C54); scroll lets the row scroll sideways without a scrollbar, as before 1.5.0 (journal behaviour-contents-bar-overflow-more)

hash.summary: When the address shows the current section, with history.replaceState, so no history entry is added: choose (the default) writes #id when a section is chosen; scroll also when the page is scrolled to one; false never. Before 1.5.0 this was a boolean and on meant scroll; true and an empty attribute now read as choose (journal behaviour-contents-hash-choose)

label.summary: The heading of the list and the navigation's accessible name; «На этой странице» / «On this page» in the page language when not set

heading-level.summary: The outline level of the list's heading (role heading, aria-level) in the column, where it is shown; the navigation is named by it in every layout

current.summary: The id of the current section: the last heading at or above the top of the scroll area (its scroll-padding-top), the last one at the end of the page; empty without sections

change.summary: The current section changed, by scrolling or by a section chosen: a fact, sent as sf-contents-change, not when the element first finds it

refresh.summary: Collects the headings of the target again (vocabulary refresh): for a page whose content changed after the contents drew

toggle.summary: Opens the sheet view's list when it is closed and closes it when it is open; refused (reason not-compact, its name kept) while the layout is not the sheet

links.$comment: Links written inside the element, text with data-level (or aria-level) for a deeper level, are read as the items when the items setting is empty; the element draws them as its list.

relations.name: cl-menu-context
relations.$comment: «Ещё (n)» of the bar opens the standard menu (overflow more), as sf-tabs' does.

relations.name: cl-badge
relations.$comment: An entry with a count or a status carries sf-badge line="text" (C95 point 6).

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: The element draws a <nav> named by its heading (aria-labelledby; the heading is role heading at heading-level, shown in the column and hidden, still naming the navigation, in the other layouts): a navigation landmark holding a list of in-page links, the current one aria-current="location". In the sheet view the list is opened by an sf-button (aria-expanded, aria-controls) named «label: current section», so its visible text is in its name; Escape closes it and gives focus back. In the rail view the names are visually hidden until hover or focus and stay the links' accessible names; where nothing hovers, the first tap on a stroke shows the names (data-open) and a tap on a name goes there. In the bar, «Ещё (n)» is an sf-button (aria-haspopup menu) after the row, opening the standard menu of the sections it holds. With fewer than two sections nothing is drawn (data-empty): a contents of one entry says nothing the page does not. The progress line is aria-hidden. An entry with a count or a status is named with it («Контакты: 2 ошибки»), its badge aria-hidden. Below md the sheet's list is a bottom sheet over a veil; opening it focuses the current entry, Escape or the veil closes it and gives focus back to the button.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-contents for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20).

rows.note: owner decision C134 (control/research/2026-11-13-navigation-density.md D5, Q1): the word compact means density only; the button view is layout sheet and writes the class sf-contents--layout-sheet beside its former sf-contents--layout-compact until the date

x-summary: The page's table of contents («Оглавление»): the sections of the page as in-page links, the current one marked while the page scrolls. Four views from one list -- a side column, the sheet (a button with the reading progress), strokes at the edge, a sticky row of anchor tabs -- and auto, the column on a wide screen and the sheet on a narrow one. It collects the headings itself or takes the items a server printed, and works as plain links without the script.

x-source.brief: simai/ui-control prototypes/docara-four.html tab 1 «Оглавление страницы» (owner-approved 2026-10-30; dispatcher decision: the name sf-contents, not sf-outline or sf-toc)

x-decisions: name: sf-contents (dispatcher, owner-delegated, 2026-10-30): the prototype said sf-outline, but outline is a CSS property and an accessibility term in the Framework (--sf-outline, the focus outline), and toc is an abbreviation. A leaf: it draws its own list of in-page links and owns no bus.

layouts: one list (<ol> of <li><a href="#id">) drawn four ways by the sheet: column, compact, rail and bar, plus auto, in the setting layout (view is reserved by the element layer, §3.1). auto is column at and above the collapse step and compact below it, one media rule per step (sm/md/lg/xl as sf-site-header's collapse), so the first paint is right without the script and nothing is measured. The script follows the same media query only to know whether the compact list can open.

data: the items setting (a server, Docara, prints them with the JSON island and the snapshot markup), else links written inside the element (the default slot, read once and drawn as the list), else the headings of target in the levels range. The printed markup is plain links, so the contents work without the script: the browser jumps to the section.

spy: an IntersectionObserver over the sections' elements (rooted at their scroll container, its top margin the container's scroll-padding-top) and a passive, frame-throttled scroll listener, both asking one question: the last section whose top is at or above the top of the scroll area, else the first; at the end of the scroll area the last section that is in view. The scroll listener also gives the compact view's reading progress. A section chosen holds the answer until its scroll ends (scrollend, else a second).

choose: a link chosen scrolls its section into view, smoothly unless prefers-reduced-motion asks otherwise (scrollIntoView respects the page's scroll-margin and scroll-padding), writes #id with history.replaceState when hash is on, and moves focus to the section (tabindex -1 when it has none) without scrolling, as an in-page link does natively.

current: a read-only value; the current link carries aria-current="location" (ARIA 1.2: the current location within a set). change is a fact of the component, x-native false: sf-contents-change {id, previous}. Not a committed value change (authoring rule: a person's committed change is the native change), and not sent for the first answer.

compact: the list opens under the button as a raised surface (elevation 2 with its text role) inside the element, not a portal and not a layer of the stack: it is a disclosure, like sf-help-mark. Escape (focus inside), a press outside and a section chosen close it; focus goes back to the button on Escape. The button is sf-button (outline, on-surface, icon-start toc, icon-end expand_more, expanded), its label the current section, its name «label: section».

rail: strokes on the length ladder (a2 tall; space-1 for level 2, space-1/2 deeper, space-3 for the current one), in --sf-outline (3:1, a non-text graphic) and the current colour; the names appear on hover of the rail and on focus within it as a raised chip (elevation 2), and stay the links' accessible names when hidden.

bar: a row of anchor tabs, sticky, on the page's surface with a region edge under it; the current tab's line is the current colour; the row scrolls sideways and keeps the current tab in view by scrolling itself, never the page.

geometry (docs/foundation-composition-geometry.md): rows are the size's text line plus a space-1/4 inset above and below in the column, the size's control height in the compact list (as a menu's rows), the compact button is sf-button of the same size; every length is a token.
css-variables: eight public variables (§6), listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json; the Framework never sets one.
words (§11): label defaults to the language files' runtime word.

version 1.1.0 compact-sticky: the compact button honours sticky as the other three layouts do. It was left out in 1.0.0, so on a phone (and under the auto step) the button scrolled away with the page; a reader who had scrolled past it had no way to the sections but scrolling back. Sticky it needs a backing, because the page scrolls under it: the host takes --sf-contents-background, else the page surface, with the band given back by a negative margin so the geometry is the one 1.0.0 measured. A page that wants the old behaviour sets sticky="false".

version 1.1.2: layout="auto" compacts below the step core/js/breakpoints.js names (SF.breakpoints, core.runtime 1.20.0), the ladder the sheet switches at, instead of a copy of it (reuse audit 2026-11-02, finding 6). The same steps.
version 1.1.3: the outcomes applied and refused come from core/js/element-manifest.js (core.runtime 1.25.0, duplication audit A-26) instead of a copy of its own; behaviour unchanged.

version 1.1.4 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.2.0 background-color-names: the public variable --sf-contents-background-color (C16 naming: a variable that sets a colour ends in -color, as the other 53 do). The former name --sf-contents-background is still read under the new one until 2027-01-01 (change journal token-component-background-color-names, src/core/contracts/token-aliases.v1.json); nothing draws differently.

version 1.3.0 (2026-11-09): the bar and the compact view's open list stand over the page: the overlay place (C20, the shadow system, owner 2026-11-08) -- --sf-shadow-overlay on the popup surface (--sf-surface-popup, a step lighter in the dark theme than the level-2 surface it had). No setting, value or event changes.

version 1.4.0 (2026-11-09): the panel declares a popup place (C16, the background system, owner 2026-11-08) (--sf-surface-place and the theme's roles back); the current entry is primary-container with its ink.

version 1.4.1 (2026-11-10): a patch; nothing in the component changed. Its built sheet is a place (sf-place) and, with C43 (component.badges 1.5.0, tokens.colour 1.8.0), takes back the core role --sf-surface-underlay with one line, --sf-surface-underlay: initial, so a tonal badge inside it lays its tone over its own surface and not over a row further out. Nothing is drawn differently outside a selected row. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.2 (2026-11-10): a patch, nothing drawn differently. The panel's last fallback background reads --sf-surface-page, the current name of the page surface (C16), where it read the former --sf-surface-0, which is var() of it everywhere; --sf-contents-background-color and --sf-contents-background still win.

version 1.4.3 (2026-11-11): a patch, nothing drawn differently. docs.md names the fallbacks of --sf-contents-background-color by their current names, --sf-surface-page and --sf-surface-popup (C16, C20), where it named the former --sf-surface-0 and --sf-elevation-2--surface; the sheet already reads them (1.4.2, 1.3.0).

version 1.5.0 (2026-11-12, owner remark R181, study control/research/2026-11-12-contents.md, defects CT-03, CT-04, CT-05, CT-09, CT-10; decision C95 point 5): a minor. CT-03: with fewer than two sections nothing is drawn -- the host says data-empty and the sheet hides the navigation, also in the printed markup (:has, no script); a host that wants its column gone reads sf-contents[data-empty]. CT-04: in the rail, where nothing hovers (a touch screen), the first tap on a stroke shows the names as the hover does (data-open; toggle does the same), and a tap on a name goes there; a tap outside, Escape or a section chosen hides them. CT-05: the bar puts the sections that do not fit into a trailing «Ещё (n)» by default (overflow more, owner decision C54 as sf-tabs), by the row engine core/js/overflow-row.js that sf-tabs' rules were taken into; the current section always stays in the row; overflow="scroll" is the former scrolling row (journal behaviour-contents-bar-overflow-more). CT-09: the heading is role heading at heading-level (default 2), not an aria-hidden span, and names the navigation by aria-labelledby, so it is in a screen reader's list of headings where it is shown. CT-10: hash is an enum, choose by default: the address is written when a section is chosen, no longer on every scroll; scroll is the former behaviour, false off; true and an empty attribute read as choose (journal behaviour-contents-hash-choose). Docara turns hash off and is not affected; a page that relied on the address following the scroll writes hash="scroll".

version 1.6.0 (2026-11-12, owner decision C95, prototype ui-control prototypes/contents-study.html, defects CT-01, CT-02, CT-06, CT-07, CT-08, CT-11, CT-12): a minor. CT-01: line="own|edge|none" says who draws the line; edge is the host's divider -- no line of the element, the 2 px current mark on its inline-start edge over the divider's pixel (the C30 / R072 e construction of a bordered menu column), so Docara's outline column needs no override of the element's classes; none draws neither. CT-02: --sf-contents-inset-inline (default --sf-space-1/2), the text's distance from the line, public; the heading and the links read it, and a host's own parts under the contents read the same value. CT-06: the current section is the surface's ink at medium weight, the primary colour on the 2 px line only (as sf-menu's column and sf-tabs), in the column and in the compact list, where it was the primary-container fill; --sf-contents-current-color colours the line, the rail's stroke and the reading line, no longer a text (journal behaviour-contents-current-line-only). CT-11: expand="all|current", all by default. CT-07: items carry count and status (error, warning, success): a badge on the entry's line, sf-badge line="text" (sf-badge 1.5.0: the height is the text's line, 16 px beside a compact entry, the number the text's size), the name says it («Контакты: 2 ошибки», words count-* and status-*), and an entry marked error goes to the first invalid field of its section ([invalid], aria-invalid, :user-invalid) and focuses it. CT-08: below md (44rem) the compact list is a bottom sheet (the screen's width up to 44rem, rounded top, the modal shadow, a veil that closes it, the safe area), rows the phone ladder's and at least the touch target under a finger; opening the list focuses the current entry's link. CT-12: the reading line lies on the compact button's own bottom edge, inside the border, inset by the corner radius, and the sticky plate has no padding below it: the element ends where the button does. Long names wrap in the rail's chips too (within --sf-f2). The default heading «На этой странице» is unchanged (C95 point 5).

version 1.6.1 (2026-11-12, owner decision C77, R191 HS-12): a patch. The text of the column and the rows of the open compact list stand at the size's value inset, the one rule of fields and lists: size 1/2 is max(--sf-space-1/2, --sf-b2), 12 on the desktop, in a compact region and on a phone, where it was --sf-space-1/2, 8; size 1 is --sf-space-1, 16 (12 compact and on a phone), where the column took 12 and the open list --sf-ui-1--space-x. --sf-contents-inset-inline defaults to it; a value a host sets is unchanged. The bar and the compact button keep their button-like side space (C76).

version 1.6.2 (2026-11-12, owner decision C109 point 2, NI-8): a patch. A deeper level steps in by the list's own inset (H4 of the horizontal-spacing standard), --sf-contents--value-inset: 12 at size 1/2 on the desktop, in a compact region and on a phone, where it was --sf-space-1/2 (8 in compact and on a phone, under the 12 inset); 16 at size 1 (12 compact and on a phone). --sf-contents-indent still sets it.

version 1.6.3 (2026-11-13, C43 D4 follow-up): a patch. In the compact view's open list the entry under the pointer is a translucent fill, as a menu's row: it names its fill to core mix sf-place-fill, so a tonal count badge on it keeps its own tone (it took the hover alpha under its own: up to 20 per channel light, 23 dark) and an anchored badge rings with the row. Nothing changes at rest. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.0 (2026-11-13): a minor (owner decision C134, control/research/2026-11-13-navigation-density.md D5/Q1: the word compact means density only, data-sf-density). The button view is layout sheet; layout compact is a dated value alias of sheet (aliases.json, the shim rewrites it and notes it once in SF.deprecations until 2027-01-01; journal value-contents-layout-compact-to-sheet). The view writes sf-contents--layout-sheet and, until the same date, its former class sf-contents--layout-compact, and the sheet draws either. Drawn the same. The host state data-compact, the getter compact and the toggle refusal reason not-compact keep their names: they are not the setting's value.

version 1.7.1 (2026-11-14): a patch, nothing drawn differently. The status mark of an entry (an sf-badge with an icon alone) writes sf-badge's icon-only, not compact, its dated alias since sf-badge 1.6.0 (owner decision C134: compact means density only; journal attribute-badge-compact-to-icon-only), so a page with a marked entry notes no deprecation of the Framework's own markup. 1.7.0 is taken by integration-fix/nav-4 (C134 layout sheet).

forbidden_client_responsibilities: styling a site's own contents list

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-contents for the table of contents of one long page: documentation, help, articles, long settings forms.
do_not: Do not use it for navigation between pages; that is sf-menu
Do not build a contents list of your own with a scroll listener
Do not put a second <nav> around it; the element is the navigation landmark

keyboard: Tab reaches each section's link in order
Enter on a link scrolls to its section and moves focus there
Enter or Space on the sheet's button opens the list; Escape closes it and gives focus back to the button
accessibility.focus: A chosen section takes focus without scrolling again (tabindex -1 when it has none), as an in-page link does natively.
